title: Protocol for generating airway organoids from 2D air liquid interface-differentiated nasal epithelia for use in a functional CFTR assay
protocol: Obtain nasal cells by nasal brushing.
Expand human nasal epithelial cells passage 0 in one well of a 12-well plate until 90% confluence is reached.
Passage HNEC p0 cells to two wells of a 6-well plate for further expansion as HNEC p1 cells.
When confluent, freeze HNEC p1 cells as a master cell bank.
Expand HNEC p2 cells on a 6-well plate for further expansion.
Freeze confluent HNEC p2 cells as a working cell bank (WCB).
Expand HNEC p3 cells from the previous step or thaw a WCB vial.
Differentiate confluent HNEC p3 cells into air-liquid interface (ALI) cultures.
Prepare a 15 mL tube with 7 mL collection medium for nasal cell brushing.
Prepare a 15 mL tube with 5 mL PBS0 for nasal cell brushing.
Inform the nasal cell donor about the procedure and intended use of the cells.
Explain that the lacrimal gland will be stimulated by the brushing procedure, which might cause tearing eyes and infrequently causes nose bleed.
Document informed consent through signing appropriate forms.
Ask the donor to blow their nose.
Instruct the donor to sit straight and sideways to the person taking the brush.
Wet the nasal brush in a tube with PBS.
Hold one hand at the back of the head to prevent head movements during the procedure.
Insert the brush horizontally into the nostril and inferior turbinate until mild resistance is felt, then turn the brush twice and remove it from the nose.
Place the brush in a 15 mL tube with collection medium, properly labeled, and keep on ice.
Repeat the procedure for the other nostril using a new brush and place it in the same 15 mL tube with collection medium.
Cut the top of the brushes and close the 15 mL tube.
Maintain the collection tube with brushes on ice or in a refrigerator.
Recoat a well in a 12-well plate as per the section “preparation: precoating of well plates for basal progenitor cell expansion”.
Prepare and pre-warm BC isolation medium in a water bath at 37°C.
Prepare freezing medium according to the section “overview of media”.
Cut the tip (approximately 0.5 cm) of a non-filter p1000 pipette tip with scissors to allow the nasal brush to fit through the opening of the tip.
Place one brush in an empty 15 mL tube.
Scrape nasal cells from the brush into the collection medium using a p1000 pipette tip.
Move the brush approximately ten times up and down through the pipette tip.
Discard the used brush after scraping.
Repeat the previous step for the second brush, reusing the cut tip if necessary.
Centrifuge the 15 mL tube with nasal cells at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant from the centrifuged sample.
Resuspend the pellet in 4 ml TrypLE express enzyme + 20 μL Sputolysin (0.5% v/v).
Be careful with aspiration when a lot of mucus is present in the pellet to prevent unintended loss of cells.
Incubate the cell suspension for 5 min at 37°C (water bath or incubator).
Resuspend the cells by pipetting up and down approximately 5 times with a p1000 pipette to dissolve mucus.
Incubate the suspension for an additional 5 min at 37°C (water bath or incubator).
Add 8 mL of Ad-DF to inactivate the TrypLE express enzyme by dilution.
Strain the cell suspension through a 100 μm cell strainer.
Wash the strainer with 2 mL Ad-DF.
Transfer half of the cell suspension to a new 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge both 15 mL tubes at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL CryoStor CS10 freezing medium (supplemented with 5 μM Y-27632).
Transfer the cell suspension to a sterile cryovial, labeled with donor number.
Gradually freeze the cells by placing the cryovials in a cell freezing container at −80°C.
Transfer the vials to a liquid nitrogen freezer after 24 h.
Aspirate the supernatant from cells in the 15 mL tube.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL BC isolation medium.
Transfer the cell suspension to a precoated well in a 12-well plate.
Label the plate, indicating passage number (p0) and donor number.
Refresh the medium three times a week with 1 mL BC isolation medium.
Change BC isolation medium for BC expansion medium after 7 days.
Culture cells until ∼90% confluence.
Coat wells in 12- or 6-well plates according to the specified section.
Prepare and pre-warm BC expansion medium in a water bath at 37°C.
Remove medium when cells are approximately 90% confluent.
Wash cells with PBS0.
For one well in a 12-well plate, add 500 μL PBS0.
For one well in a 6-well plate, add 1000 μL PBS0.
After removal of PBS0, add TrypLE express enzyme to the cells.
For one well in a 12-well plate, add 500 μL TrypLE express enzyme.
For one well in a 6-well plate, add 1000 μL TrypLE express enzyme.
Incubate the cells with TrypLE at 37°C until they detach.
Incubate for an additional 5 minutes.
Pipette TrypLE up and down a few times to detach all cells from the well.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL tube.
Wash the well with Ad-DF to remove remaining cells.
Transfer the wash solution to the 15 mL tube to inactivate the TrypLE.
Determine cell numbers using a cell counter.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove collagen solution or PBS from precoated wells.
Transfer cells dissolved in BC expansion medium to these wells.
For one well in a 12-well plate, add 0.2 × 10^6 cells to 1 mL BC expansion medium.
For one well in a 6-well plate, add 0.5 × 10^6 cells to 2 mL BC expansion medium.
Refresh the medium three times a week with BC expansion medium until further notice.
Refresh the culture medium for one well in a 12-well plate with 1 mL BC expansion medium.
Refresh the culture medium for one well in a 6-well plate with 2 mL BC expansion medium.
Detach basal progenitor cells from the well plate after expansion.
Determine cell concentration with a cell counter.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in CryoStor CS10 freezing medium (containing Y-27632) to obtain a final concentration of 1–2 × 10^6 cells per mL.
Divide 0.5 mL of the cell suspension over sterile cryovials, each containing 0.5–1 × 10^6 cells.
Label the cyrovials, indicating passage number and donor number.
Place the labeled cyrovials in a cell freezing container at -80°C.
Transfer the cells from the -80°C freezer to a liquid nitrogen freezer as soon as possible after reaching -80°C.
Take a cryovial with cells from the liquid nitrogen freezer and store on dry ice if not processed immediately.
Store the cryovial in the -80°C freezer for a maximum of 14 days if processing is delayed.
Place the cryovial in a 37°C water bath until the cell suspension is almost thawed.
Rapidly transfer the thawed cell suspension to a 15 mL tube containing 5 mL Ad-DF.
Wash the cryovial with 1 mL of Ad-DF.
Add the washed contents to a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove collagen solution or PBS0 from precoated wells.
Transfer cells dissolved in BC expansion medium to these wells.
For one well in a 12-well plate, add 1 mL of BC expansion medium.
For one well in a 6-well plate, add 2 mL of BC expansion medium.
Refresh cell cultures three times a week with BC expansion medium.
For one well in a 12-well plate, refresh with 1 mL of BC expansion medium.
For one well in a 6-well plate, refresh with 2 mL of BC expansion medium.
Coat Transwell inserts according to the specified section.
Prepare and pre-warm ALI-diff medium.
Transfer basal progenitor cells to transwell inserts.
Dissociate basal progenitor cells from a well plate as per step 41–46 of the specified protocol.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the coating solution from the Transwell inserts.
Seed basal progenitor cells on the apical side of the Transwell inserts.
Add BC expansion medium to the basolateral side.
Refresh the medium three times a week and culture the cells under submerged conditions until full confluence is reached.
When confluent, change apical and basolateral medium for ALI-diff phase 1 medium (ALI-diff medium supplemented with A83-01 (500 nM)).
Refresh the medium three times a week until a homogeneous monolayer exists with all cells having similar size and morphology.
Remove medium from the apical side and culture the cells under air-exposed conditions.
Change basolateral medium to ALI-diff phase 2 medium (ALI-diff medium supplemented with A83-01 (500 nM) and neuregulin-1β (0.5 nM)).
Add 600 μL of ALI-diff phase 2 medium for 6.5 mm inserts in a 24-well plate.
Add 1 mL of ALI-diff phase 2 medium for 12 mm inserts in a 12-well plate.
After 3–5 days, replace basolateral medium with ALI-diff phase 3 medium (ALI-diff medium supplemented with neuregulin-1β (0.5 nM)).
Refresh the basolateral medium twice a week.
Wash the cells once a week at the apical surface.
Incubate with PBS0 in a tissue incubator at 37°C for 5–10 minutes.
For 6.5 mm inserts (24-well plate), wash with 125 μL PBS0.
For 12 mm inserts (12-well plate), wash with 200 μL PBS0.
Proceed to the next step when beating cilia are observed under a light microscope.
Detach the ALI-differentiated epithelial cell layer from the Transwell insert using collagenase.
Manually disrupt and strain the epithelial sheets to generate 30–100 μm fragments.
Pre-warm 24-well suspension plates in a tissue incubator for at least 24 hours.
Thaw Matrigel on ice or at 4°C.
Prepare and pre-warm AO culture medium.
Wash the differentiated ALI-cultures at the apical surface with PBS0.
Incubate for 5 minutes in a tissue incubator.
Add collagenase type II solution (1 mg/mL in Ad-DF) to the basolateral side of the ALI-culture.
Incubate for 45–60 minutes in a tissue incubator.
Add Ad-DF to the apical surface of the Transwell insert and transfer the dissociated epithelial layer to a 15 mL tube.
Add 100 μL Ad-DF per Transwell insert for 6.5 mm inserts (24-well plate).
Add 200 μL Ad-DF per Transwell insert for 12 mm inserts (12-well plate).
Wash the apical side of the Transwell insert with Ad-DF.
Transfer remaining epithelial fragments to a 15 mL tube containing the epithelial layer.
Disrupt the epithelial layer into smaller fragments using a P1000 pipet tip.
Evaluate the size of the epithelial fragments by eye or light microscope.
The majority of the epithelial fragments should have a diameter of approximately 30–100 μm.
Obtain small fragments, an additional P200 non-filter tip can be placed on top of the P1000 pipet tip.
Strain the epithelial fragments with a combination of a 100 μm pluriStrainer® placed on top of a 30 μm pluriStrainer®.
Add 4 ml Ad-DF to the 15 ml tube containing epithelial fragments, and transfer the fragments through the strainers.
Discard the 100 μm strainer.
Flip the 30 μm strainer upside down on top of a new 50 ml tube.
Add 5 ml Ad-DF to the reversed 30 μm pluriStrainer® to collect the epithelial fragments in the 50 ml tube.
Wash both sides of the 100 μm and 30 μm pluriStrainers® with 1 ml Ad-DF before use.
Transfer the epithelial fragments to a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 400 g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant.
Add 60 μL of Matrigel for epithelial fragments from a 6.5 mm 24-well insert, or add 180 μL of Matrigel for epithelial fragments from a 12 mm 12-well insert.
Mix well on ice to prevent solidification of the Matrigel.
Avoid formation of bubbles during resuspension in Matrigel.
Place a pre-warmed 24-well suspension plate on top of a T175 flask filled with handwarm tap water.
Apply 30 μL droplets per well.
Flip the plate upside down after 2 minutes.
Solidify the droplets in a tissue incubator for 15–30 minutes.
Add 500 μL of pre-warmed AO culture medium to the epithelial fragments embedded in Matrigel.
Refresh the medium twice a week, adding it gently to avoid disruption of the Matrigel droplets.
Passage nasal organoids to a 96-well plate after lumen formation.
Thaw Matrigel on ice or at 4°C.
Prepare and pre-warm AO culture medium.
Remove culture medium from wells.
Add 400 μL of cell recovery solution per well.
Resuspend the Matrigel droplet in cell recovery solution once.
Incubate the well plate at 4°C for 5–10 minutes until Matrigel is dissolved.
Transfer organoids to a 15 mL tube with 7 mL ice cold Ad-DF.
Keep the tube on ice.
Centrifuge the organoids at 400 g and 4°C for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant from the tube.
Resuspend the organoid pellet in 100% Matrigel.
Keep the tube on ice.
Determine plating volume based on amount of wells to be seeded plus 10% extra volume.
Plate organoids into 96-well plates using a test droplet and check density under light microscope.
Take a pre-warmed 96-well plate and add 4 μL Matrigel droplets with organoids in each well.
Regularly resuspend the organoids in the Eppendorf tube to keep a homogeneous suspension.
Tap the 96-well plate regularly on a flat surface during plating (± after every 16–24 wells) to distribute the organoids in the same plane.
Solidify the Matrigel droplets by placing the plate in a tissue incubator for 15–25 min.
Add 100 μL AO culture medium to each well and place the plate in a tissue incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Replace organoid medium with 100 μL pre-warmed AO FIS assay medium, 5–10 days prior to the FIS assay.
Refresh the organoid medium with 100 μL AO FIS assay medium supplemented with CFTR correctors (i.e., VX-809, VX-445, VX-661; 5 μM) or vehicle control, 48 hours prior to the FIS assay.
Turn on the environmental control of the confocal microscope at least 1 hour before starting the experiment at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Dissolve calcein green (50 μg) in 6 μL DMSO.
Prepare a calcein green solution (1:750 v/v) in Ad-DF (10 μL/well).
Prepare 2× concentrated dilutions of compounds to be added acutely: i.e., forskolin (10 μM), CFTR potentiators (VX-770; 10 μM) or vehicle in Ad-DF.
Dispense 125 μL of the compound solutions per well in a new U-bottom 96-well suspension plate.
Dispense 10 μL of calcein green solution to each well of the 96-well plate containing organoids.
Mix the calcein green solution through gentle resuspension (2–3 times pipetting) with a multichannel.
Incubate the plate in a tissue incubator for 30 min.
Position the 96-well plate with organoids in the place holder of a confocal microscope and ensure the plate is fixed in position.
Set the live cell imaging settings using the 2.5× objective.
Use an emission at 488 nm and excitation at 515 nm for calcein green staining.
Ensure that the calcein green signal in the organoid structures is slightly oversaturated by setting the laser intensity appropriately.
Set the right position (X, Y) and focus (Z) for each well to obtain a good view of the organoids or use autofocus when possible.
Set a time lapse for 1 h measurement with an interval of 10 min and cycles of 7 (cycle 1 is t = 0).
Add 100 μL from the 96-well plate with acute stimuli to the well plate.
Immediately start imaging after addition of the acute stimuli.
